newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 7.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- In one of the most systematic and wounding attacks ever uttered in the English High Courts, counsel for former Irish Prime Minister Albert Reynolds described Ireland's Labour Party programme manager Fergus Finlay as a fixer who had turned chicken by not giving evidence in the liber action against the Sunday Times.
- The man at the centre of the Northern Ireland peace talks, George Mitchell, may be promoted to the most powerful position in President Clinton's cabinet, as the Secretary of State.

- Ireland's government is facing a major embarrassment on Thursday following the overnight release and re-arrest of 15 high security prisoners from Portlaoise, Mountjoy and Limerick jails due to a legal hitch.

- Twelve of the 15 members of the European Union, including Ireland, are expected to qualify for membership of the single European currency next year, the European Commission said in an upbeat report on the union's economic condition.
- The rise in sterling to parity with the Irish pound could add around half a percent to Irish inflation next year, Ireland's Davy Stockbrokers say.

- Falling international interest rates have shielded the Irish government from the full impact of its borrow and spend policies, say Ireland's Bloxham Stockbrokers in their latest financial market report.

- The country's new national station Radio Ireland on Wednesday announced a deal with Ireland's national broadcasting station, RTE, which will allow it broadcast to 97 percent of the population using 19 new transmitters costing 1.3 million punts.

- Wholesale changes are on the way in recently re-elected President Clinton's cabinet and this could bring former Senator George Mitchell back to Washington from chairing the Northern Ireland multi-party talks.
- Two men were being questioned by Irish police in Dublin on Wednesday, and three in Cork, in connection with a search of a freighter in Bantry Bay.

- The political director of Ireland's Labour Party, Fergus Finlay, on Wednesday rejected remarks about him made during the closing statement by Lord Gareth Williams QC in the "Sunday Times' libel action in London on Wednesday.

- Ireland's Minister for Social Welfare and leader of the Democratic Left, Proinsias De Rossa, outlined his teenage life as a republican under cross-examination on the second day of his court action alleging libel against the "Sunday Independent.'
- There will be no sudden drop in European Union funding for Ireland post-1999, EU Commissioner, Monika Wulf-Mathies, has confirmed.

- Oil and petrol prices are expected to fall by half-a-penny a litre (2.27p a gallon) as a result of the Irish government's decision to modify the arrangement between oil importers and the Whitegate oil refinery.
